feature_overview.business_goal: let logged-in users browse the available items/products in one place so they can see what's in stock before deciding what to look into further — this is a browsing/catalog view, not a management tool.
scope: Displaying a list of sample items with basic details (name, description, price, quantity, category).
Handling loading and error states for the item listing.
feature_overview.feature_boundary: This Architecture Plan covers only the Item Listing feature and excludes unrelated features.

functional_requirements.description: Only authenticated (logged-in) users can access the Item Listing page; an unauthenticated user is redirected to the login page.
The page displays a list of items, each showing its name, description, price, quantity, and category.
The database is pre-seeded with at least 8-10 sample items so the page has real content to show immediately, with no manual data entry needed first.
If there are no items, the page shows a clear empty state ('No items found').
While items are loading, the page shows a loading indicator; if the fetch fails, it shows a clear error message instead of a blank page.
A link to the Item Listing page is added to the site's main navigation so a logged-in user can reach it.
The system must separate product catalog data from inventory data to prevent overselling and ensure accurate stock levels.
The system must use stock movement logs instead of silent quantity updates to track changes in inventory accurately.
The system must display product availability clearly to customers, indicating whether an item is in stock or out of stock.

pages.purpose: Main page for the Item Listing feature. UI expectations: A clean grid or table layout consistent with the rest of the app's existing styling.; Responsive on both desktop and mobile widths.

implementation_order: Create app/api/items/route.ts implementing /api/items, validating required request fields before use (400 on missing/malformed) -- it is automatically live the instant the file exists, no separate mount step needed.
Create lib/api/itemListing.ts with one function per endpoint.
Create app/item-listing/page.tsx (a Client Component, `"use client"` as its first line), reusing approved UI/UX components where available instead of re-authoring their markup.
Register a real <Link href="/item-listing"> in app/page.tsx at the FEATURE_LINKS markers -- a page with no link to it is not complete.
constraints: The Next.js App Router scaffold already exists and works -- never recreate app/layout.tsx, next.config.mjs, tsconfig.json, or lib/mongodb.ts.
A Route Handler (route.ts) is live the instant it exists -- there is no router to mount it on, unlike an Express app.js.
Register new pages by adding a real <Link href="..."> in app/page.tsx (FEATURE_LINKS markers) -- an unreachable page is not done.
Every Mongoose model file must use the `mongoose.models.X || mongoose.model(...)` guard to avoid OverwriteModelError.

Approved UI/UX output is a visual reference, not code to import -- use read_ui_component_design/read_ui_page_design to see the approved HTML+Tailwind design, then write real TSX that faithfully matches its structure/classes/content.
